use_case_summary: WillowBend is building an embeddable chat widget for mid-market e-commerce merchants. Primary traffic: synchronous chat for shoppers (low-latency, single-turn and multi-turn), supplemental doc search for help center and automated summary emails. Expect bursty traffic at marketing pushes and holiday windows. Wants hosted, self-serve flow but needs predictable quota controls and clear retry guidance.
notes:
Early-stage SMB inbound. Team of ~12 engineers, product-led launch planned in 8-10 weeks. Main contact Tess (PM) + Austin (backend lead). Key convo points:
- They can sign up self-serve and liked the SDKs; no dedicated contract needed for initial phase.
- Pain: spikes during promotional emails produced 429s in their PoC — they want guardrails: per-key concurrency caps, burst buckets, and clear guidance for exponential backoff + jitter.
- "We don't want to babysit rate limits during Black Friday style spikes" — Tess on call.
- Wants simple admin UI to raise quotas temporarily for a campaign; also wants usage alerts (email/Slack) when approaching quota.
- Security: SSO for admin, audit logs for API key usage; not doing on-prem.
- Cost sensitivity: SMB budget, looking for predictable billed units; asked about per-request vs per-token and how burst usage is billed.
- Technical asks from Austin: recommended concurrency limit settings for chat widgets, sample token bucket configs, best-effort fallback model suggestions when primary hits rate limit.
- Agreed next step: provide a 1-page "burst handling playbook" (include client retry snippet + server-side quota options) and demo snippet they can drop into the widget. Aim to convert to paid in Q2 if PoC resolves 429s and pricing acceptable.
